advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the compose-up jgit.config guard section-aware (verify receive.autogc=false, e.g. via `git config --file`) instead of a section-blind line grep.
evidence: infra/scripts/compose-up.sh:225:   echo "compose-up: FATAL — infra/compose/jgit.config must keep receive.autogc=false" >&2
The regex is section-blind: git-config semantics scope `autogc` to its enclosing section header, but the grep never checks that `[receive]` precedes the matched line.
advisory.finding: The compose-up sanity check greps for 'autogc = false' on ANY line of jgit.config without confirming it is under the [receive] section; a mislocated or wrong-section 'autogc = false' would pass while receive.autogc is missing/true, yet the FATAL message asserts 'receive.autogc=false' is guaranteed.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the grep with `git config --file "${SITE_HOST_DIR}/etc/jgit.config" --bool --get receive.autogc` and assert the value is `false`, so the check honors git-config section scoping.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document (or narrow) the mirror-fetch refspec: warn that `--prune '+refs/heads/*:...'` can delete/force-reset live Gerrit branches diverging from the GitHub mirror.
evidence: `--prune` with a force `+refs/heads/*:refs/heads/*` refspec deletes local refs/heads not on the mirror and force-overwrites divergent ones; the runbook frames this only as backfilling missing objects.
advisory.finding: Runbook step 3's mirror fetch uses `--prune '+refs/heads/*:refs/heads/*'`, force-updating and pruning all of the live Gerrit repo's refs/heads/* from the GitHub mirror; branches present in Gerrit but absent from GitHub would be deleted and divergent branches force-reset, a data-loss hazard the runbook does not call out.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a behavior test that runs compose-up.sh (copy + PATH-stubbed siblings) to confirm it seeds etc/jgit.config and aborts with exit 1 when jgit.config is missing receive.autogc=false.
evidence: tests/scripts/test_gerrit_object_store_repair.py:32-35: `text = _COMPOSE_UP.read_text(); assert "infra/compose/jgit.config" in text; assert "${SITE_HOST_DIR}/etc/jgit.config" in text; assert "receive.autogc=false" in text`

infra/scripts/compose-up.sh:223-226: `cp "${REPO_ROOT}/infra/compose/jgit.config" "${SITE_HOST_DIR}/etc/jgit.config"` then `grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*autogc[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*false...' ... || { echo "compose-up: FATAL ..." >&2; exit 1; }` — the exit-1 guard whose behavior is never executed by a test

tests/scripts/test_docker_storage_cap.py:504-528 and tests/scripts/test_journald_cap.py:331-348: existing pattern that copies compose-up.sh, stubs siblings via PATH, runs it, and asserts behavior from a call log — the harness this test could use to actually seed and to trigger the fail-loud abort
advisory.finding: test_compose_mounts_and_seeds_jgit_config asserts source-text substrings of compose-up.sh ('${SITE_HOST_DIR}/etc/jgit.config', 'receive.autogc=false') rather than driving the added seed+guard behavior. The newly-added fail-loud guard (`grep -qE ... autogc ... false ... || { echo FATAL; exit 1; }`, compose-up.sh lines 224-226) has an abort path that no test exercises, and the grep would break on a behavior-preserving rename of SITE_HOST_DIR or restructure of the seed step.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Drive the jgit.config detect-only signal by adding ('infra/compose/jgit.config', None) to _CONFIG_MANUAL_SOURCES in test_autodeploy_signals_gerrit_config.py rather than grepping autodeploy.sh text.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:218: `# infra/compose/gerrit.config and infra/compose/jgit.config are in this list, NOT in a` (path present in a comment, so the grep is satisfied by the comment alone)
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:232: CONFIG_PATHS='... infra/compose/gerrit.config infra/compose/jgit.config' (the real gating membership the test fails to isolate)

tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_signals_gerrit_config.py:45-48,116-146: existing harness drives the REAL autodeploy.sh under a PATH shim and asserts the emitted AUTODEPLOY_ERROR reason=config_manual signal per detect-only source — the behavior-verifying pattern this grep should have joined
blocking.finding: test_autodeploy_flags_jgit_config_for_manual_apply only asserts the substring 'infra/compose/jgit.config' appears anywhere in autodeploy.sh text, but that path is present both in a COMMENT (line 218) and in CONFIG_PATHS (line 232); the test therefore passes even if jgit.config is dropped from CONFIG_PATHS (which would silence the detect-only signal) as long as it stays in the comment. The newly-introduced detect-only behavior (a jgit.config change emits AUTODEPLOY_ERROR reason=config_manual) is never exercised.
blocking.suggested_fix: In tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_signals_gerrit_config.py add a parametrize case `("infra/compose/jgit.config", None)` to `_CONFIG_MANUAL_SOURCES`, so the existing harness runs autodeploy.sh and asserts AUTODEPLOY_ERROR reason=config_manual fires for a jgit.config-only change; drop or downgrade the substring grep.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Change the runbook's for-each-ref verification to assert a non-empty count (or check exit status) rather than redirecting all output to /dev/null.
evidence: Output is discarded and there is no `|| exit`/count assertion; the step's positive result is indistinguishable from the command running against an empty/wrong repo or failing silently.
dropped.finding: Runbook step 5's repository ref-enumeration 'verification' pipes for-each-ref to /dev/null and never checks its exit status, so it produces no observable signal — an operator cannot distinguish 'refs enumerated cleanly' from 'produced nothing / command errored'.
